mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 0.5% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 4.0% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 4.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and rising inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes real corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong month-over-month increase in personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) combined with a weaker increase in personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals a rise in savings rate, suggesting future demand uncertainty and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-mo MA AND GDPC1 < PAYEMS growth rate
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS grows faster than GDPC1 in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for two consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as markets anticipate central bank tightening.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE falls below 3.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent month-over-month decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 6-month average for three consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST is below its 6-month moving average for three consecutive months.
